entries.actual_author: J. B. S. Haldane, not Feynman
entries.work: Possible Worlds (1927): 'the Universe is not only queerer than we suppose, but queerer than we can suppose'
entries.notes: Audit: SOURCE DISPLACEMENT. Ascriptions to Heisenberg, Eddington and Priestley are all post-1927 and spurious. Recorded in the census as the specimen where verification had to overturn the AUDITOR'S OWN PRIOR, not only the manuscript's claim - I had believed the line was Heisenberg's.
Wording exact including the second sentence.

entries.actual_author: Rumi, rendered by Coleman Barks with John Moyne
entries.work: The Essential Rumi (HarperCollins), copyright 1995 Coleman Barks
entries.translator_or_mediator: Coleman Barks - NOT NAMED in the manuscript, which carries a bare byline
entries.notes: Audit: a LOOSE RENDERING, not a translation - Barks renders the Persian terms for kufr and islam as 'wrongdoing' and 'rightdoing'. Verbatim use of a mediator's English under a bare byline; contrast the correctly labelled 'Adapted from Rumi, after Coleman Barks' item in Ch5.

Audit: the original reads 'Beware of HIS false knowledge', following 'A learned man is an idler who kills time with study'. The standalone form was standardised by Laurence J. Peter's Peter's Quotations (1977). Snopes rates the attribution correct. Same author as the reattributed Whyte item - two Shaw occurrences, opposite outcomes.

entries.match: An open mind leaves a chance
entries.notes: Audit: absent from twainquotes.com and from Wikiquote's sourced Twain sections. Twain is a magnet for unsourced attribution.

entries.work: proposed editions: A Monk in the World and The Mystic Heart - not located in either
entries.notes: Audit: UNVERIFIED - source lead unresolved. Teasdale is a real author and the thought matches his interspiritual, engaged-monastic thesis exactly. THEMATIC FIT PROVES NOTHING.

entries.work: The Return of Collective Intelligence (Bear & Company, 2020) - subject matches, sentence not located
entries.notes: Audit: Dyer is a real author, former editor of Costa Rica's Tico Times.

entries.actual_author: unknown - competing attribution to Edward Everett Hale
entries.notes: Audit: UNVERIFIED, UNKNOWN. Shows BOTH instability markers at once - a competing attribution (Hale, 1822-1909, whose death predates the attribution) and no primary source.

entries.work: documented original in Paul Brooks, The House of Life: Rachel Carson at Work (1972)
entries.notes: Audit: EVOLVED APHORISM / RECOVERABLE ANCESTOR. A documented Carson original exists and the manuscript's wording departs from it.

entries.work: SOURCE LEAD: Mark Jenkins, The Hard Way (2003)
entries.notes: Audit: UNVERIFIED, origin UNKNOWN, with a source lead. WITHDRAWN AS AN INTERNAL-ORIGIN CANDIDATE - it had been flagged on conceptual fit with the book's own thesis, and the external source trail dissolved that. Specimen for the rule that external-circulation search runs BEFORE the internal-origin flag, not after.

entries.match: seek to discover the best in others
entries.notes: Audit: Ward (1921-1994) is a real and heavily anthologised writer of inspirational maxims; the line is consistently his, but no work or page is attested.

entries.match: ability to reach unity in diversity
entries.bibliography_relationship: 'Young India' cited without volume or date
entries.notes: Audit: quote-site attestation only. Needs checking against the Collected Works of Mahatma Gandhi.

entries.match: Our own decision to view the universe
entries.notes: Audit: not located in Wikiquote, Goodreads, or the organism.earth McKenna transcript archive - a substantial searchable library of his talks. ABSENCE THERE IS MORE MEANINGFUL THAN ABSENCE FROM QUOTE SITES (corpus-density principle).

entries.match: past is a place of reference
entries.bibliography_relationship: CORRECT - third correctly-supported citation in Ch8
entries.notes: Audit: confirmed on the author's own publication channel, which meets the official-source standard. The census records its own correction here: Bennett had been flagged as a figure of uncertain identity because the book is an aphorism collection, and that suspicion-by-genre was withdrawn.

entries.match: only thing worse than being blind
entries.notes: Audit: UNVERIFIED, origin UNKNOWN. No primary source locatable for this wording, and it sits inside a FAMILY OF COMPETING PHRASINGS - the signature of a saying polished in transmission.

entries.match: Intelligence is the ability to adapt
entries.actual_author: not Stephen Hawking - nearest ancestor is a Leon C. Megginson paraphrase of Darwin (1963)
entries.notes: Audit: no evidence Hawking said it; the Washington Post ran a piece specifically investigating the attribution (2018). The Megginson paraphrase later hardened into a pseudo-Darwin quotation.

SECOND OCCURRENCE, still active. The Ch6 occurrence was removed at 4A; this one survives because 4A's scope was section-opening epigraphs and the two occurrences differ in function. Audit: not located in the Aristotelian corpus; quote sites variously credit Aristotle, Plato, Socrates and Laozi. The underlying maxim is the Delphic 'Know thyself'.

entries.match: Alone we can do so little
entries.notes: Second occurrence of the same saying, Ch8. Spoken line documented in Lash, Helen and Teacher (1980).

historical_entries.notes: Ch6 occurrence, removed at 4A. Its Ch8 twin is STILL ACTIVE - same misattributed saying, verbatim, same attribution. Family link added so the surviving occurrence cannot be lost sight of.
